title: The Holy Spirit at Ephesus, Demetrius and the Riot

questions.question: In Ephesus, Paul found about twelve disciples who had only received John's baptism. After he baptized them in the name of the Lord Jesus and laid his hands on them, what happened?
options: The Holy Spirit came on them, and they began speaking in tongues and prophesying
They fell to the ground and wept with deep repentance
They spoke in tongues and then immediately were baptized again
They were filled with joy and immediately went out to preach
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy Spirit came on them, and they began speaking in tongues and prophesying
questions.explanation: Acts 19:6 (ESV): "And when Paul had laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them, and they began speaking in tongues and prophesying."

questions.question: Paul reasoned in the synagogue for three months. When some were stubborn and spoke evil of the Way, he withdrew. Where did he then hold daily discussions?
options: The hall of Tyrannus
The home of Aquila and Priscilla
The marketplace of Ephesus
A classroom in the Jewish academy
questions.explanation: Acts 19:9 (ESV): "...he withdrew from them and took the disciples with him, reasoning daily in the hall of Tyrannus."

questions.question: For how long did Paul hold discussions in the hall of Tyrannus?
options: Two years
Three years
One year
Eighteen months
questions.explanation: Acts 19:10 (ESV): "This continued for two years, so that all the residents of Asia heard the word of the Lord, both Jews and Greeks."

questions.question: God was doing extraordinary miracles through Paul. What objects that had touched Paul were used for healing and deliverance?
options: Handkerchiefs or aprons
His cloak and sandals
Pieces of cloth he had woven
Small clay tablets he had blessed
questions.explanation: Acts 19:12 (ESV): "so that even handkerchiefs or aprons that had touched his skin were carried away to the sick, and their diseases left them and the evil spirits came out of them."

questions.question: Seven sons of a Jewish high priest named Sceva tried to cast out a demon by invoking the name of Jesus and Paul. What happened?
options: The evil spirit said "Jesus I know, and Paul I recognize, but who are you?" Then the man leaped on them and overpowered them, and they fled wounded
The demon was cast out but then returned with seven worse spirits
The men were struck dumb for seven days as punishment
The demon laughed at them and then fell silent at God's command
questions.correctAnswer: The evil spirit said "Jesus I know, and Paul I recognize, but who are you?" Then the man leaped on them and overpowered them, and they fled wounded
questions.explanation: Acts 19:15-16 (ESV): "But the evil spirit answered them, 'Jesus I know, and Paul I recognize, but who are you?' And the man in whom was the evil spirit leaped on them, mastered all of them and overpowered them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded."

questions.question: Many who had practiced magic arts brought their books together and burned them. What was the total value of these books?
options: Fifty thousand pieces of silver
One hundred thousand denarii
Thirty thousand shekels of silver
Five thousand pieces of gold
questions.explanation: Acts 19:19 (ESV): "And a number of those who had practiced magic arts brought their books together and burned them in the sight of all. And they counted the value of them and found it came to fifty thousand pieces of silver."

questions.question: Demetrius the silversmith made silver shrines of Artemis. Why did he stir up his fellow craftsmen against Paul?
options: Paul's preaching was causing the trade of making shrines to Artemis to be at risk, since people were turning away from the goddess
Paul had publicly insulted Artemis in the theater
The Roman proconsul had given Paul authority to suppress idol worship
Paul had refused to buy a silver shrine as a gift for the church
questions.correctAnswer: Paul's preaching was causing the trade of making shrines to Artemis to be at risk, since people were turning away from the goddess
questions.explanation: Acts 19:25-27 (ESV): "Men, you know that from this business we have our wealth. And you see and hear that not only in Ephesus but in almost all of Asia this Paul has persuaded and turned away a great many people..."

questions.question: The crowd in the theater at Ephesus was in confusion, chanting "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!" for about how long?
options: About two hours
About one hour
About three hours
For half a day
questions.explanation: Acts 19:34 (ESV): "But when they recognized that he was a Jew, for about two hours they all cried out with one voice, 'Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!'"

questions.question: Two of Paul's companions were dragged into the theater during the riot. Who were they?
options: Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians who traveled with Paul
Silas and Timothy who had joined him in Ephesus
Trophimus and Tychicus, Paul's fellow workers
Aquila and Priscilla who lived in Ephesus
questions.correctAnswer: Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians who traveled with Paul
questions.explanation: Acts 19:29 (ESV): "So the city was filled with the confusion, and they rushed together into the theater, dragging with them Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians who were Paul's companions in travel."

questions.question: Who eventually quieted the crowd and dismissed the assembly in Ephesus?
options: The town clerk
The proconsul of Asia
Paul himself
The chief priests of Artemis
questions.explanation: Acts 19:35-41 (ESV): "And when the town clerk had quieted the crowd, he said..."

questions.question: The town clerk noted that if Demetrius had a complaint, there were courts and proconsuls. He dismissed the assembly saying they were in danger of being charged with what?
options: Rioting, since there was no cause for this commotion
Treason against Rome for not stopping the Christian movement earlier
Blasphemy for claiming Artemis was greater than other gods
Sedition for interfering with lawful religious practice
questions.correctAnswer: Rioting, since there was no cause for this commotion
questions.explanation: Acts 19:40 (ESV): "For we really are in danger of being charged with rioting today, since there is no cause that we can give to justify this commotion."

questions.question: Paul had resolved in the Spirit to pass through Macedonia and Achaia and go to Jerusalem, saying "After I have been there, I must also see..."?
options: Rome
Spain
Alexandria
Antioch
questions.explanation: Acts 19:21 (ESV): "Now after these events Paul resolved in the Spirit to pass through Macedonia and Achaia and go to Jerusalem, saying, 'After I have been there, I must also see Rome.'"

questions.question: Alexander was pushed forward by the Jews to address the crowd. What happened when they saw he was a Jew?
options: They shouted him down with the Artemis chant for two hours
They listened but then began to argue among themselves
They threw things at him and he fled the theater
They listened respectfully but then rejected his arguments
questions.correctAnswer: They shouted him down with the Artemis chant for two hours
questions.explanation: Acts 19:34 (ESV): "But when they recognized that he was a Jew, for about two hours they all cried out with one voice, 'Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!'"

questions.question: The word of the Lord continued to increase and prevail mightily following the burning of the books. This summary describes what period?
options: The conclusion of Paul's two-year Ephesian ministry
The beginning of Paul's third missionary journey
The period after Apollos had strengthened the Ephesian church
The time following the Jerusalem council's decision
questions.correctAnswer: The conclusion of Paul's two-year Ephesian ministry
questions.explanation: Acts 19:20 (ESV): "So the word of the Lord continued to increase and prevail mightily." This came at the end of the extended Ephesian period described in Acts 19.

questions.question: The town clerk in Ephesus defended that Gaius and Aristarchus were not "sacrilegious" and had not "blasphemed" their goddess. What does this suggest about Paul's method of evangelism?
options: Paul confronted idolatry by proclaiming truth rather than publicly insulting pagan religion
Paul had successfully avoided all controversy in Ephesus
Paul had paid bribes to officials to protect his companions
Paul's ministry was so underground it attracted little official notice
questions.correctAnswer: Paul confronted idolatry by proclaiming truth rather than publicly insulting pagan religion
questions.explanation: Acts 19:37 (ESV): "For you have brought these men here who are neither sacrilegious nor blasphemers of our goddess." This implies Paul proclaimed truth without resorting to direct insults of Artemis.

key_verse_text: So the word of the Lord continued to increase and prevail mightily.
